title.title: Failure of Kohn–Sham ensemble representation
title.subtitle: Claim: a three-electron molecule whose ground-state density no noninteracting ensemble reproduces

beats.text: Three electrons, two equal nuclear charges $Z$ (given by an exact formula)
Kohn–Sham DFT assumes noninteracting electrons can reproduce every such density
Claim: this one cannot, for any potential in $L^{3/2} + L^\infty$

achievement.label: Kohn–Sham ensemble representability
achievement.context: Counterexample: a three-electron molecule with two equal positive-integer nuclear charges
achievement.note: One potential class only; the nuclear charge is likely huge

verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

sources.quote: three-electron Coulomb molecule with two equal positive-integer nuclear charges
the nuclear charge is specified only by a formula (likely huge)

plain: Chemistry software assumes any electron cloud can be copied by simpler, non-interacting electrons. Not always

steps: The theory assumes every density comes from simpler electrons
Build a molecule: three electrons, two equal nuclei
Its density matches no such system: the assumption fails

voice.text: Can independent electrons in some potential reproduce its density?
Build this exact molecule; no potential makes simpler electrons match its density.
Claimed: this density cannot be reproduced.
